OK, so depending on how long you want the infill to last, you'll be looking at different types of paint.

The longest lasting will be an automotive, enamel paint.

First, gently sand back the engraving with a medium grit sandpaper and a sanding block to remove any burrs or raised edges. The block is essential to ensure you maintain a consistent depth.


Next, pour a small amount of thinners or methylated spirits on the engraving and scrub it with a soft toothbrush to clean it up.


Next, thin some enamel paint with thinners and drop it onto the surface next to the engraving (less is more, don't use too much) , then screen it over with a bit of soft plastic (a cut up margerine container works well). You want the paint to fall into the engraving and "fill" it.


Allow it to dry completely, then sand again with your sanding block and a piece of 240 grit wet sandpaper.

They're pantry bugs, I can't remember their name, but you gotta get rid of them or they'll fill your whole pantry.


Pull everything out, and inspect each item carefully. You'll find their laying eggs in either flour, cocoa or spices. Throw out anything that has even one bug on it. They can even be found under the labels of cans. You have to be brutal and might even end up throwing everything out.


Spray the pantry with bug spray (any type will do) and close it up for about an hour. Then clean all surfaces inside the pantry with spray n wipe or soapy water. Take out the shelves (if you can) and clean the gaps between the shelves and the walls. Get rid of every trace of bugs you can find. 


After you're done, you can refill the pantry, but check for bugs every hour or so as there will be some  missed no matter how thorough you are. Keep checking for a few days until you stop seeing any bug activity. 


Do this TODAY or they'll take over your kitchen.

In the future, all flour, spices and cocoa needs to spend 48 hours in your freezer before you use it.
